actions.name: Send Bulk Chats

arguments.name: Account
arguments.description: WhatsApp account you want to use for sending. You can get the account unique ID from /get/wa.accounts or in the dashboard.

arguments.name: Campaign
arguments.description: Name of the campaign, you will see this in the WhatsApp campaign manager.

arguments.name: Recipients
arguments.description: List of phone numbers or group addresses separated by commas. Optional if 'groups' parameter is not empty. Accepts WhatsApp group address, E.164 formatted number, or locally formatted numbers using the country code from your profile settings.

arguments.name: Groups
arguments.description: List of contact group IDs separated by commas. Optional if 'recipients' parameter is not empty. You can get group IDs from /get/groups (Your contact groups).

arguments.name: Type
arguments.description: Type of WhatsApp message.

arguments.name: Message
arguments.description: Message or caption you want to send. Spintax and shortcodes are supported.

arguments.name: Media File
arguments.description: For 'media' type messages only. The media file to attach to the WhatsApp message. Supports jpg, png, gif, mp4, mp3, and ogg files.

arguments.name: Media Url
arguments.description: For 'media' type messages only. URL to the media file. Must be a direct link. Supports jpg, png, gif, mp4, mp3, and ogg files.

arguments.name: Media Type
arguments.description: For 'media' type messages only. Required if using 'media_url' instead of 'media_file'. Declares the file type of the media in the provided URL.

arguments.name: Document File
arguments.description: For 'document' type messages only. The document file to attach to the WhatsApp message. Supports pdf, xml, xls, xlsx, doc, and docx files.

arguments.name: Document Url
arguments.description: For 'document' type messages only. URL to the document file. Must be a direct link. Supports pdf, xml, xls, xlsx, doc, and docx files.

arguments.name: Document Name
arguments.description: For 'document' type messages with 'document_url'. File name of the document. Include the file extension (e.g., document.pdf).

arguments.name: Document Type
arguments.description: For 'document' type messages only. Required if using 'document_url' instead of 'document_file'. Declares the file type of the document in the provided URL.

arguments.name: Shortener
arguments.description: Shortener ID. Specify the shortener to use for shortening links in your message. Get the list of available shorteners from /get/shorteners.

actions.name: Send Bulk SMS
actions.description: Sends bulk SMS messages from WhatsBoost.

arguments.name: Mode
arguments.description: Mode of sending the message, it can be 'devices' which will allow you to use your linked android devices or 'credits' which will allow you to use gateways and partner devices. 'credits' requires you to have enough credit balance to send messages.

arguments.name: Campaign
arguments.description: Name of the campaign, you will see this in the SMS campaign manager.

arguments.name: Numbers
arguments.description: List of phone numbers separated by commas. It can be optional if 'groups' parameter is not empty. It will accept E.164 formatted numbers or locally formatted numbers using the country code from your profile settings. E.164: +34612345678 Local: 612345678.

arguments.name: Groups
arguments.description: List of contact group ID's separated by commas. It can be optional if 'numbers' parameter is not empty. You can get group ID's from /get/groups (Your contact groups).

arguments.name: Message
arguments.description: Message you want to send, spintax and shortcodes are supported.

arguments.name: Device
arguments.description: Linked device unique ID, this is required if you will send with 'devices' mode. You can get linked device unique ID from /get/devices (Your devices).

arguments.name: Gateway
arguments.description: Partner device unique ID or gateway ID, this is required if you will send with 'credits' mode. You can get a partner device unique ID and gateway ID from /get/rates.

arguments.name: Sim
arguments.description: SIM slot number you want to use. For 'devices' mode only.

arguments.name: Priority
arguments.description: Priority level. 0 or 1 = high priority (sent immediately), 2 = normal priority (queued). For 'devices' mode only.

arguments.name: Shortener
arguments.description: Shortener ID, specify the shortener you want to use if you want to shorten the links in your message. You can get the list of available shorteners from /get/shorteners.

setupGuide.title: Connect Whautomate
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Whautomate account with access to Integrations > REST API. This draft currently supports only the global host https://api.whautomate.com.

steps.title: Open REST API settings in Whautomate
steps.description: Sign in to your Whautomate account, open Integrations, then choose REST API settings.

steps.title: Confirm your account uses the global API host
steps.description: Check that the API host shown in your REST API settings is https://api.whautomate.com before continuing.

steps.title: Generate an API key
steps.description: Select New API Key, enter a label such as Whautomate API, generate the key, then copy it.

name: WooCommerce
description: Manage WooCommerce products, orders, customers, and store settings

authentication.name: Consumer Key + Secret (Basic Auth)
authentication.description: Authenticate with your WooCommerce store URL, consumer key, and consumer secret over HTTPS.

credentials.name: Site URL
credentials.description: Base URL of your WooCommerce store (for example https://example.com).

setupGuide.title: Connect your WooCommerce store
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need WordPress admin access to the store and an HTTPS store URL.

steps.title: Open WooCommerce REST API keys
steps.description: In your WordPress admin, go to WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API keys. This is the screen where WooCommerce lets you create and manage REST API keys.

steps.title: Create a new API key
steps.description: Select Create an API key or Add key. Enter a description, choose the WordPress user the key belongs to, and choose the access level. Use Read for read-only actions, or Read/Write if you plan to use write actions later.

steps.title: Copy the values into MindCloud
steps.description: Enter your store URL in Site URL. Paste the Consumer Key into Username and the Consumer Secret into Password.
